assessments.technical_explanation: The flagged link-like literals are loopback URLs used by the end-to-end test harness to reach the temporary HTTP server it starts on a random local port. All network activity stays on the machine running the test; no external destination, credential, or untrusted input appears in this flow, and the file is test automation rather than shipped extension code.
assessments.layman_explanation: The test starts its own tiny web page on the tester's own computer to click through the extension's interface. The web addresses it uses point back to that same machine, not to the internet or any outside service.

assessments.technical_explanation: The signal matches a CommonJS-style module resolution inside a test harness, needed because the test file uses ES modules. The resolution target defaults to the standard Playwright browser-automation package, with an environment variable override for pointing CI at a local install. The file runs only under developer or CI automation, is not shipped with the extension, and the loaded module is the browser driver the test drives.
assessments.layman_explanation: The test loads the browser automation tool it needs to simulate clicking through the interface. That tool comes from the project's own test setup, and an optional configuration setting lets automated test runs point at a specific local copy.

assessments.technical_explanation: The supplied source is fully readable unit-test code: ordinary imports of the project's own modules and the Node test runner, plain assertions, and descriptive Korean test names. There is no encoded payload, dynamic evaluation, packed string, or hidden logic anywhere in the shown file; the low-confidence obfuscation signal is a false positive, most plausibly triggered by the non-ASCII text, emoji, and unusual string fixtures used as test data.
assessments.layman_explanation: The file is ordinary, readable test code with no attempt to hide what it does. The alert appears to be a machine misreading of the plain text, which includes emoji and Korean sample content used as test data.

assessments.technical_explanation: The signal matches a read of a single environment variable used as the module path for the browser driver in the test harness. The file never serializes the process environment, and no environment values are logged, persisted, or sent to any destination. Reading one test configuration variable in an automation-only test file is not credential handling or exfiltration.
assessments.layman_explanation: The test reads one configuration setting from the machine's environment to locate its browser tool. It does not collect, save, or transmit any environment values, and this file never runs on a user's install of the extension.
